title: White frames appear when adding BrowserView with already loaded page
body: I'm using Electron 20.1.4 on macOS Ventura 13.2 x64. When I add a BrowserView whose page is already loaded to a BrowserWindow, one or more white frames appear even though the window has another background color. It works as expected on Windows 11, and the white glitch is not reproducible when I call app.disableHardwareAcceleration(). I need this for native-looking tab switching and would like either a fix or a workaround.

symptoms_visible: On macOS, adding a BrowserView with an already loaded page briefly shows white frames even though the BrowserWindow has a different background color.
The same operation looks correct on Windows 11, and I do not see the white glitch when hardware acceleration is disabled.
N0.label: N0 white frames reported

symptoms_visible: Keeping the BrowserViews attached and changing their order avoids the white flash, but transparent pages remain visible over one another.
N1_x.label: N1_x keep-views-attached aftermath

symptoms_visible: The white glitch appears whenever I add a loaded BrowserView on top of another view, and it can also be reproduced by repeatedly removing and re-adding one loaded BrowserView.
Keeping multiple BrowserViews attached makes transparent pages overlap and consumes more resources.
N2.label: N2 minimal reproduction and rendering errors collected

symptoms_visible: Moving the newly attached view off-screen and moving it back after a short delay can look correct on a high-end Mac, but white glitches still appear on lower-end Macs.
N3_x.label: N3_x bounds-delay workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: My custom BrowserView replacement API using fallback content still shows the white glitch.
Waiting 100 ms after attachment before showing the new contents appears smooth on my test machine, but I do not have a paint event to use instead of the fixed delay.
N4_x.label: N4_x custom replacement aftermath

symptoms_visible: A maintainer reports that the issue is fixed and no longer reproducible on current stable Electron versions; I have not reported a retest on my own system.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix shipped, reporter verification pending

solution.intent: Keep all BrowserViews attached and switch their stacking order with addBrowserView and setTopBrowserView instead of removing and re-adding them.
solution.concrete_example: Add each BrowserView once, then call setTopBrowserView for the active tab; alternatively, move inactive views outside the window bounds.

edges.comment: c0-c1, reporter's macOS system: the suggested addBrowserView plus setTopBrowserView technique avoids flashing, but the reporter demonstrates that transparent pages overlay each other, so it is not acceptable for the stated tab-switching use case.

question_patterns: Does keeping the views attached and switching them with addBrowserView and setTopBrowserView avoid the flash?
What happens if you leave both BrowserViews attached and only change which one is on top?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: addBrowserView plus setTopBrowserView avoids the flash, but some pages have transparent backgrounds, so the pages overlay each other. That is not desired.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Keeping the views attached works cleanly: none of my pages are transparent, memory use is acceptable, and there is no flash.
The stacking technique removes the flash, but only a few of my pages show transparent overlap.

question_patterns: Why can't you keep every tab's BrowserView attached?
Besides transparent overlap, is there another reason the attached-view workaround is unsuitable?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I measured higher resource consumption when the window has multiple BrowserViews attached at the same time. I want inactive tab views detached.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Resource use is the same with every BrowserView attached, and I can make all page backgrounds opaque.

edges.comment: c0-c6: the reporter tested the stacking suggestion, later supplied a one-BrowserView remove/re-add reproduction and explained the resource constraint. A second affected contributor's raw SharedImageManager and invalid-mailbox log lines are folded into the simulated user side and enter N2 as volunteered evidence; they are not interpreted as a proven mechanism.

question_patterns: Why is leaving all BrowserViews attached not viable for your application?
Can you reduce the problem to one BrowserView that is removed and re-added?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I measured higher resource consumption with multiple attached BrowserViews. I can reproduce the white glitch with one loaded BrowserView by removing it and adding the same instance back after one second.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot reproduce it with one BrowserView; it only happens when several transparent views overlap.
The one-view reproduction uses a half-second delay rather than one second and shows the same flash.

edges.comment: c3-c6, reporter's system plus folded affected contributor: after rejecting the keep-attached workaround, the reporter supplies a minimal one-view reproduction. The second contributor independently records the raw mailbox errors during each flicker.

solution.intent: Hide the newly reattached BrowserView outside the window, wait briefly, and then move it to its visible bounds.
solution.concrete_example: After addBrowserView, set its bounds to x: 800, wait about 20 ms, and then set its bounds back to x: 0.

edges.comment: c7-c8, affected contributor folded into the simulated user side: the off-screen setBounds timeout appears effective on a high-end Mac, but further testing shows that white glitches remain on lower-end devices, falsifying it as a reliable workaround.

solution.intent: Implement a single BrowserView replacement operation in a custom Electron build and transfer fallback content while replacing the old view.
solution.concrete_example: Use a custom replaceBrowserView(oldView, newView) implementation that calls TakeFallbackContentFrom rather than separately removing and adding the views.

edges.comment: c11-c12, reporter's custom Electron build: the reporter implements ReplaceBrowserView with TakeFallbackContentFrom, but says it is not enough to eliminate the glitch. A separate 100 ms delayed reveal appears to work locally but remains a timing-dependent hack without a paint-ready signal.

solution.intent: Update to a current stable Electron build containing the linked upstream fix, reproduce the same loaded-BrowserView attachment sequence with hardware acceleration enabled, and ask the reporter to verify the result before declaring the case resolved.
solution.concrete_example: The maintainer reports that the linked Electron change fixed this and that it is no longer reproducible on latest stable versions. Upgrade from Electron 20.1.4, rerun the one-view remove/re-add gist on macOS with hardware acceleration enabled, and report whether any white frame remains.
solution.inference_hint: The thread establishes only that a linked upstream Electron change fixed the issue and that a maintainer could no longer reproduce it on current stable builds. It does not describe the change's internal mechanism. The invalid overlay-mailbox log lines and hardware-acceleration dependence support a rendering-path diagnosis, but they do not justify inventing a more precise root cause.

edges.comment: c29-c30: an Electron maintainer states that the issue was fixed by the linked upstream change and is no longer reproducible on latest stable versions. OldDream celebrates the result but does not explicitly report testing it, and the original reporter never confirms a retest; therefore the terminal state records a shipped fix with reporter verification still pending.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted issue at the level established by the thread: an Electron BrowserView rendering bug on macOS when an already loaded view is attached or reattached with hardware acceleration enabled; the thread does not establish a more precise internal root cause.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the one-BrowserView remove/re-add reproduction, the hardware-acceleration dependency, and the raw non-existent overlay-mailbox and invalid-mailbox errors.
Must recommend updating to a current stable Electron build containing the linked upstream fix and retesting the original loaded-BrowserView attachment sequence with hardware acceleration enabled.
Must not present keeping every BrowserView attached as a complete fix because transparent pages overlap and the reporter measured increased resource use.

Must not rely on off-screen bounds changes, hard-coded reveal delays, or the custom fallback-content replacement as a reliable fix; those approaches were device-sensitive or still exhibited the white glitch.

Must ask the affected reporter to verify a build containing the fix before declaring the issue resolved; the thread contains a maintainer's no-longer-reproducible report but no explicit reporter retest.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Electron application developer who can produce minimal Fiddle-style reproductions, inspect Electron and Chromium source, build a custom Electron fork, and prototype native BrowserView APIs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, persistent, and highly technical; supplies reduced code samples and measurements, explains product constraints, and asks maintainers for robust alternatives to timing-based hacks.
